sentences.en: No, no, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: It's incredible also how I think this is one of the interesting things and nice things about GPU programming is that an algorithm that can be so simple to understand and so intuitive as a rotate can get so complicated when it comes to implementing it,
sentences.zh: 同时这也令人难以置信，我认为这是GPU编程最有趣、最美妙的方面之一：一个在理解上如此简单、像旋转（rotate）这样直观的算法，在实际实现时却会变得如此复杂，

sentences.en: if you want to achieve the best performance.
sentences.zh: 如果你想追求极致的性能的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's basically the beauty of GPU programming that everything is so intricate.
sentences.zh: 是的，这基本上就是GPU编程的魅力所在，一切都如此错综复杂。

sentences.en: I mean, it's definitely a property of GPU programming.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对是GPU编程的一个特性。

sentences.en: But if you think about the implementation of rotate on the CPU, like it's very, very complex as well.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细想想在CPU上实现rotate，比如它其实也非常非常复杂。

sentences.en: Like before I knew about iterator category tag dispatching, you think it's just a bunch of swaps, which I guess it is at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 就像在我了解迭代器类别标签分派（iterator category tag dispatching）之前，你可能会觉得它只是一堆交换操作，我想归根结底确实如此。

sentences.en: But depending on the iterator category, it's dispatching to like a bunch of different implementations.
sentences.zh: 但根据迭代器类别的不同，它会被分派到一堆不同的实现中去。

sentences.en: Anyway, so just like rotate visually very simple, but like, not just on the GPU, but also on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 总之，rotate从视觉上看非常简单，但不仅在GPU上，在CPU上也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, it's like the algorithm rabbit hole that never ends.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就好比是一个永远走不出的算法兔子洞。

sentences.en: So do you want to do a recap on why we needed a long algorithm and how the short algorithm works?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们想回顾一下为什么我们需要长算法以及短算法是如何工作的吗？

sentences.en: Let's do that.
sentences.zh: 我们就这么办吧。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: In the short algorithm,
sentences.zh: 在短算法中，

sentences.en: it's called short because you're assuming that the rotate distance is going to be less than the size of the tile that you use for tiling the array for parallelizing the memory movement.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫短算法，是因为你假设旋转距离（rotate distance）将小于你用来对数组进行分块以并行化内存移动的切片（tile）的大小。

sentences.en: And so in the short algorithm, how it works is that each block of threads is going to get a tile starting from the back of the array and moving forwards.
sentences.zh: 所以在短算法中，它的工作原理是：每个线程块（thread block）将从数组的尾部开始向前获取一个切片。

sentences.en: And then they get a tile.
sentences.zh: 然后他们获取一个切片。

sentences.en: They cache it into shared memory.
sentences.zh: 将其缓存到共享内存（shared memory）中。

sentences.en: They set a flag flagging that that tile has been cached and another thread block can overwrite that memory location.
sentences.zh: 他们设置一个标志，标明该切片已被缓存，这样另一个线程块就可以覆盖该内存位置。

sentences.en: And then they look at the flag of the tile that they are going to overwrite to make sure that they are not overwriting memory that has not been read yet.
sentences.zh: 然后，他们查看即将覆盖的切片的标志，以确保他们没有覆盖尚未被读取的内存。

sentences.en: And then they can store the tile in its destination and move on to the next tile.
sentences.zh: 接着，他们可以将切片存储到其目标位置，并继续处理下一个切片。

sentences.en: And so since you're moving the tiles in a spatial order from the back forwards,
sentences.zh: 因此，由于你是按空间顺序从后向前移动切片的，

sentences.en: in a situation where your rotate distance is large enough that you cannot cover that rotate distance with the amount of tiles that you're processing at the same time,
sentences.zh: 在你的旋转距离足够大，以至于你无法通过同时处理的切片数量来覆盖该旋转距离的情况下，

sentences.en: you're going to have a deadlock because all of your blocks of threads that are waiting for the flags to be released in order to store something are going to be waiting indefinitely because there's not enough blocks running in order to make that work.
sentences.zh: 就会产生死锁，因为所有等待释放标志以便存储数据的线程块都将无限期地等待下去，因为没有足够运行中的线程块来让它正常工作。

sentences.en: This is a very interesting property of this particular algorithm, you know, that if you you have this linear parameter, how much you're going to shift by.
sentences.zh: 这是这个特定算法一个非常有趣的特性，你知道，如果你有这样一个线性参数，即你要偏移多少。

sentences.en: And if you go over a certain size, then you have to switch to a completely different implementation strategy.
sentences.zh: 如果你超过了一定的大小，那么你就必须切换到一个完全不同的实现策略。

sentences.en: And that that's that shift point is like going to be some unintuitive number that's just like a property of the underlying hardware and the underlying degree of concurrency.
sentences.zh: 而那个转变点将是一个不那么直观的数字，它仅仅底层硬件和底层并发度的一个属性。

sentences.en: That's I just find that's like a very fascinating property.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一个非常迷人的特性。

sentences.en: I don't think that any of our other core algorithms have a similar property and that they have some linear parameter like this that just so it's like it's almost like you tell me that there's these two very different implementations.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们的其他核心算法有类似特性，即它们具有这样一个线性参数，以至于——这几乎就像你告诉我这里有两种非常不同的实现。

sentences.en: It's almost as if the maybe one could imagine them, they're different algorithms, you know, like in other circumstances where it's not a linear parameter,
sentences.zh: 这就好像人们可以想象它们是不同的算法，你知道，在其他情况下，如果它不是一个线性参数，

sentences.en: we would probably have two different named algorithMs.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会有两个不同名称的算法。

sentences.en: But in this case, because the interface, like there's no reason to surface this in the interface because it's just this like linear parameter.
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，由于接口方面——没有理由在接口中暴露这一点，因为它只是这样一个线性参数。

sentences.en: Like why if it's, you know, a thousand versus a thousand and one, do I need to call a completely different API?
sentences.zh: 为什么如果它是，比如说，一千和一千零一的区别，我就需要调用一个完全不同的API？

sentences.en: It's just fascinating to to to I really think this is very unique in our parallel algorithms library design.
sentences.zh: 这真的很令人着迷，我真的认为这在我们的并行算法库设计中是非常独特的。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe there's some other analogy that I that you can think of that I can't.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也许你能想到其他我想不到的类比。

sentences.en: No, no, I agree with you.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我同意你的看法。

sentences.en: It's incredible also how I think this is one of the interesting things and nice things about GPU programming is that an algorithm that can be so simple to understand and so intuitive as a rotate can get so complicated when it comes to implementing it.
sentences.zh: 同时这也令人难以置信，我认为这是GPU编程最有趣、最美妙的方面之一：一个在理解上如此简单、像旋转这样直观的算法，在实际实现时却会变得如此复杂，

sentences.en: If you want to achieve the best performance.
sentences.zh: 如果你想追求极致的性能的话。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's basically the beauty of GPU programming that everything is so intricate.
sentences.zh: 是的，这基本上就是GPU编程的魅力所在，一切都如此错综复杂。

sentences.en: Well, I think it's you can almost I mean, that's definitely a property of GPU programming.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想你可以几乎——我的意思是，这绝对是GPU编程的一个特性。

sentences.en: But if you think about the implementation of rotate on the CPU, like it's very, very complex as well.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细想想在CPU上实现rotate，比如它其实也非常非常复杂。

sentences.en: Like before I knew about iterator category tag dispatching, you think it's just a bunch of swaps, which I guess it is at the end of the day.
sentences.zh: 就像在我了解迭代器类别标签分派之前，你可能会觉得它只是一堆交换操作，我想归根结底确实如此。

sentences.en: But depending on the iterator category, it's dispatching to like a bunch of different implementations of which, you know, the generalization of GCD, which, you know,
sentences.zh: 但根据迭代器类别的不同，它会被分派到一堆不同的实现中去，其中，你知道，GCD（最大公约数）的泛化，你知道的，

sentences.en: I've gotten comments on videos before is like GCD isn't used for anything.
sentences.zh: 我以前在视频下看到过评论说“GCD什么也用不上”。

sentences.en: It's like, well, it's actually used for a lot of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，嗯，实际上它用在了很多地方。

sentences.en: And it's and it's not just on integers.
sentences.zh: 而且它不仅适用于整数。

sentences.en: You can think of it on like sequence lengths.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它应用到序列长度上。

sentences.en: And anyway, so just like rotate visually, very simple, but like not just on the GPU, but also on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 总之，rotate从视觉上看非常简单，但不仅在GPU上，在CPU上也是如此。

sentences.en: You know, it's like the the algorithm rabbit hole that never ends.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就好比是一个永远走不出的算法兔子洞。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah, for sure.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对，确实如此。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, so that's basically that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，基本就是这样。

sentences.en: And then you need to switch to the long algorithm.
sentences.zh: 然后你需要切换到长算法。

sentences.en: And so actually, it's very similar, quite similar in terms of the memory movement and the implementation.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在内存移动和实现方面，它与短算法非常相似。

sentences.en: It's just that now you no longer process the tiles in spatial order, because if you did that, you would deadlock.
sentences.zh: 只是现在你不再按空间顺序处理切片了，因为如果你那样做，就会产生死锁。

sentences.en: And so now you need to say, you know, let's say we start at the tile that's at the back.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你需要说，比方说，我们从位于尾部的切片开始。

sentences.en: Then we know that the tile that's at the back, it's going to overwrite the tile that's wherever.
sentences.zh: 然后我们知道，位于尾部的那个切片，将去覆盖某个地方的切片。

sentences.en: And then that tile is going to overwrite another tile.
sentences.zh: 接着那个切片又会去覆盖另一个切片。

sentences.en: And so you start creating this dependency chain of how do you need to process tiles in order to minimize the distance between them whenever processing and minimize the possibility of a deadlock.
sentences.zh: 于是你开始创建这样一个依赖链：为了在处理时尽量缩短它们之间的距离并最大程度减少死锁的可能性，你应该如何处理切片。

sentences.en: Yeah, so now, of course, now that our rotate distance is large, we also need to tile the part that we are moving into the back.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以现在，当然，既然我们的旋转距离很大，我们也需要对我们要移到背部的部分进行切片。

sentences.en: So in the short algorithm, since we knew that our rotate distance was less than the size of a tile, we wouldn't bother with that.
sentences.zh: 所以在短算法中，既然我们知道旋转距离小于切片大小，我们就不会费心去处理这个了。

sentences.en: We just said, OK, the last tile in the ones that we're processing is the one that takes care of moving the first elements into the back.
sentences.zh: 我们只是说，好吧，在我们正在处理的切片中，最后一个切片负责把最前面的元素移到后面去。

sentences.en: But now, since our rotate distance is large, we also need to tile all of the elements that go into the back, because that's now a big part of our array.
sentences.zh: 但现在，既然我们的旋转距离很大，我们也需要对所有移到后部的元素进行切片，因为这现在是我们数组的很大一部分。

sentences.en: And we would lose a lot of performance if we did it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不这样做，就会损失大量的性能。

sentences.en: And so now, in the implementation, those tiles that are going to be rotated into the back are going to be negative tiles.
sentences.zh: 所以在实现中，那些将被旋转到后部的切片将是负数切片。

sentences.en: So the tile that starts at the beginning of the array is tile minus 1, and then you go to tile minus 2, minus 3, minus 4,
sentences.zh: 因此，从数组开头开始的切片是切片-1，然后是切片-2、-3、-4，

sentences.en: until you get to the boundary where the rotate distance is.
sentences.zh: 一直到旋转距离所在的边界。

sentences.en: And then you start with the positive tiles, which start at 0, and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后你从正数切片开始，它们从0开始，依此类推。

sentences.en: And so how the implementation now works is that you create a dependency map, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 现在的实现原理是，你创建一个所谓的依赖图（dependency map）。

sentences.en: So you calculate, this is basically a mathematical calculation, where if you know the array size, the tile size, and the rotate distance, for any tile,
sentences.zh: 所以你进行计算，这基本上是一个数学计算：如果你知道数组大小、切片大小和旋转距离，对于任何一个切片，

sentences.en: you can mathematically find out which tiles it is going to overwrite.
sentences.zh: 你都可以通过数学方法找出它将要覆盖哪些切片。

sentences.en: So which memory location it is going to overwrite.
sentences.zh: 也就是它将要覆盖哪个内存位置。

sentences.en: And so you do that for every tile.
sentences.zh: 你对每个切片都这样做。

sentences.en: And once you have that, you basically start at tile 0.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了这个，你基本上从切片0开始。

sentences.en: And let's say tile 0 overwrites tile minus 1 and tile minus 2.
sentences.zh: 假设切片0覆盖了切片-1和切片-2。

sentences.en: Then, since you know that it's going to overwrite those, you start at tile 0, and then you go on to minus 1.
sentences.zh: 然后，既然你知道它会覆盖这些，你就从切片0开始，接着转向-1。

sentences.en: And then you see, okay, which tile does tile minus 1 overwrite?
sentences.zh: 然后你看看，好吧，切片-1覆盖了哪个切片？

sentences.en: It overwrites tile 30.
sentences.zh: 它覆盖了切片30。

sentences.en: And so you jump to tile 30.
sentences.zh: 于是你跳转到切片30。

sentences.en: And then tile 30 overwrites tile 50, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后切片30覆盖了切片50，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And you do that, and so you have this dependency chain that you follow until you've covered all of the tiles.
sentences.zh: 你重复这个过程，这样你就拥有了这条依赖链，一直跟着它走，直到遍历了所有的切片。

sentences.en: And so you do this on the CPU, and then you pass this, you copy this array onto the GPU.
sentences.zh: 你在CPU上完成这一步，然后将这个数组传递、复制到GPU上。

sentences.en: And so now, instead of processing the tiles in spatial order, you process these tiles along the dependency chain.
sentences.zh: 因此，现在你不再按空间顺序处理切片，而是沿着依赖链来处理这些切片。

sentences.en: And so that way, you're minimizing the possibility of a deadlock.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，你可以最大限度地减少死锁的可能性。

sentences.en: And so this is basically the only change.
sentences.zh: 基本上这就是唯一的改变。

sentences.en: In terms of the memory movement, it's the same.
sentences.zh: 在内存移动方面，它是相同的。

sentences.en: It's the same in terms of that you cache into shared memory.
sentences.zh: 在缓存到共享内存这一点上也是相同的。

sentences.en: You free the overwrite flag, and then you look at your dependencies overwrite flags in order to write to the destination.
sentences.zh: 你释放覆盖标志，然后查看依赖项的覆盖标志，以便写入目标位置。

sentences.en: What changes is how you process the tiles and in which order you do that.
sentences.zh: 改变的是你如何处理切片以及以什么顺序去处理。

sentences.en: But this is also another interesting thing, that it's also not impervious to deadlocking.
sentences.zh: 但这也是另一个有趣的事情，它也并非完全不会死锁。

sentences.en: Because for certain array sizes and rotate distances,
sentences.zh: 因为对于某些数组大小和旋转距离，

sentences.en: you can get a dependency chain where the distance between one tile and its furthest dependency that it needs to be freed in order to overwrite is actually larger than the number of third blocks that you have on your GPU resident.
sentences.zh: 你会得到这样一条依赖链：某个切片与为了能够被覆盖而必须被释放的最远依赖项之间的距离，实际上大于你在GPU上驻留的线程块数量。

sentences.en: So you would, again, have a deadlock.
sentences.zh: 所以，你又会遇到死锁。

sentences.en: And so you actually need a third implementation that is then the naive implementation where you just do it naively.
sentences.zh: 因此，你实际上需要第三种实现，也就是朴素实现（naive implementation），直接用最简单的方法来做。

sentences.en: You just do the rotate by copying the first element into a scratch buffer.
sentences.zh: 你只需通过将第一个元素复制到临时缓冲区（scratch buffer）来执行旋转。

sentences.en: You lost me on the third one.
sentences.zh: 第三种把我给听懵了。

sentences.en: I'm not seeing the deadlock.
sentences.zh: 我没看出死锁是怎么回事。

sentences.en: Can you explain this to me again?
sentences.zh: 你能再给我解释一遍吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So you understand how now we're using this dependency chain so that we process them in the order that they are going to be needed to be processed, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 所以你理解我们现在是如何使用这个依赖链的吧，这样我们就可以按照它们需要被处理的顺序来处理它们，可以这么说。

sentences.en: Because if tile 0 is overwriting tile minus 1 and tile minus 2, for it to be able to overwrite them and not deadlock, after a thread block grabs tile 0,
sentences.zh: 因为如果切片0正在覆盖切片-1和切片-2，为了让它能够覆盖它们而不死锁，在一个线程块获取了切片0之后，

sentences.en: you want the next thread blocks to grab tiles minus 1 and minus 2, so that you free up tile 0 and it can move on and store it to its location.
sentences.zh: 你希望接下来的线程块去获取切片-1和切片-2，这样你就能释放切片0，它就可以继续前进并将其存储到它的位置上。

sentences.en: And so that's the concept of the dependency graph.
sentences.zh: 这就是依赖图的概念。

sentences.en: That you get the concept of that.
sentences.zh: 你懂这个概念了对吧。

sentences.en: Do you have a visual?
sentences.zh: 你有图解吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: I know we're not supposed to ask in the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们不应该在播客里问这个。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The listener is going to have to visualize it, but I can show you a visual.
sentences.zh: 听众们将不得不靠想象来理解，但我可以给你看一个图解。

sentences.en: The listener may not be as tired as I am.
sentences.zh: 听众可能没有我这么累。

sentences.en: Connor, maybe please can give me an exception.
sentences.zh: 康纳，或许能给我个特例吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I was thinking that, you know how Wikipedia, for at least the sort algorithms, they have all these really nice animations.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我在想，你看维基百科上，至少对于排序算法，他们都有这些非常棒的动画。

sentences.en: Of like, you know, merge sort or bubble sort.
sentences.zh: 比如归并排序或冒泡排序。

sentences.en: That it's an equivalent animation for the two different implementations here that show the tiles being, you know, copied in the dependency order would probably be, like,
sentences.zh: 如果这里针对这两种不同的实现有一个对应的动画，展示切片按依赖顺序被复制的过程，那可能——

sentences.en: an order of magnitude easier if you could show that in a podcast, which you cannot.
sentences.zh: 如果你能在播客中展示这一点的话，会简单一个数量级，但你做不到。

sentences.en: I mean, we could if we had a video format, but we don't right now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们有视频格式就可以，但我们现在没有。

sentences.en: So, I mean, technically this is being recorded.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，严格来说这正在录音中。

sentences.en: We've talked about it.
sentences.zh: 我们已经讨论过它了。

sentences.en: We've talked about it.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过了。

sentences.en: We have, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们讨论过了。

sentences.en: Once both Bryce and I retire and, you know, whenever that is, a couple decades, maybe we'll add video.
sentences.zh: 一旦布莱斯和我双双退休——不管那是什么时候，几十年后吧，也许我们会加上视频。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, you can see the screen.
sentences.zh: 所以，你能看到屏幕。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, I guess, basically, I can describe what we're seeing.
sentences.zh: 那么，我想，基本上我可以描述我们所看到的内容。

sentences.en: So, we're seeing an array that has 10 tiles.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们看到一个包含10个切片的数组。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: And we want to rotate it by three and a half tiles.
sentences.zh: 我们想把它旋转三个半切片的大小。

sentences.en: And so, how we do this is that we first create this dependency table where each tile is going to have, if you think of it as a hash map,
sentences.zh: 我们是这样做的：首先创建这个依赖表，其中每个切片都将拥有——如果你把它想象成一个哈希表（hash map），

sentences.en: the tile number is going to be the key and the value is going to be a list of the tiles that that tile overwrites.
sentences.zh: 切片编号将是键（key），而值（value）将是该切片所覆盖的切片列表。

sentences.en: So, for example, since tile 0 is always going to be going into the front of the array because it's the first one after our rotate distance,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，由于切片0总是会进入数组的前端，因为它在我们旋转距离之后的第一个切片，

sentences.en: it is always going to be overwriting tile minus 1, which is the first tile at the beginning of the array.
sentences.zh: 它总是会覆盖切片负1，也就是数组开头的第一个切片。

sentences.en: And so, the key would be tile 0 and the value would be tile minus 1.
sentences.zh: 所以，键将是切片0，值将是切片负1。

sentences.en: And so, if we do this for all of our tiles, we now have our dependency map, and we now start the dependency chain in tile 0.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们对所有切片都这样做，我们现在就有了依赖关系图，然后我们从切片0开始依赖链。

sentences.en: And so, tile 0, as we've said, overwrites tile minus 1.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们所说，切片0会覆盖切片负1。

sentences.en: And so, we add that one into our dependency chain.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们将它加入到我们的依赖链中。

sentences.en: And then we look at tile minus 1, and then from accessing the hash map, we see that it overwrites tile 3 in our example.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看切片负1，从访问哈希表中，我们看到在我们的例子中它覆盖了切片3。

sentences.en: And so, we add tile 3 to our processing order or to our dependency graph.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们将切片3加入到我们的处理顺序或依赖图中。

sentences.en: And then we look at tile 3, and tile 3 overwrites tiles minus 4 and tile 0.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看切片3，切片3覆盖了切片负4和切片0。

sentences.en: And so, we add minus 4.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们加入负4。

sentences.en: But since tile 0 has already been processed earlier, we don't need to add it again, so we don't add it.
sentences.zh: 但由于切片0之前已经被处理过了，我们不需要再次添加它，所以我们不添加它。

sentences.en: And then we look at tile minus 4, and we do that on and on.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看切片负4，以此类推。

sentences.en: What does processing mean?
sentences.zh: 什么是处理？

sentences.en: So, if 0 depends on negative 1, then how do you process 0 before negative 1?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果0依赖于负1，那你怎么能在负1之前处理0呢？

sentences.en: No, well, 0 depends on negative 1 in the sense that in order for the thread block that has grabbed tile 0 to be able to continue with its processing,
sentences.zh: 不，嗯，0依赖于负1的意思是，为了让已经获取了切片0的线程块能够继续处理，

sentences.en: it needs someone, some other thread block, to have grabbed tile minus 1 and have cached it.
sentences.zh: 它需要某个其他的线程块来获取切片负1并将其缓存。

sentences.en: Because if not, it's going to overwrite whatever was here.
sentences.zh: 因为如果不这样，它就会覆盖这里原本的内容。

sentences.en: So, after you grab tile 0, then you're waiting for somebody to grab tile negative 1?
sentences.zh: 所以，在你获取了切片0之后，你就在等待别人去获取切片负1？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Okay, and so, this is just the processing order is to make this go faster.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以，这只是说处理顺序是为了让这个过程更快。

sentences.en: Well, it's to make this go faster, but also to make it not deadlock.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是为了让它更快，但也是为了不发生死锁。

sentences.en: Because imagine in our example that we only had three processors.
sentences.zh: 因为想象一下在我们的例子中，如果我们只有三个处理器。

sentences.en: And let's say we started in the front, just to make it simple.
sentences.zh: 假设我们从前面开始，为了简单起见。

sentences.en: Then we would grab tiles minus 1, minus 2, minus 3.
sentences.zh: 那么我们会获取切片负1、负2、负3。

sentences.en: But tile minus 1 would be wanting to overwrite something that no other processor is grabbing.
sentences.zh: 但是切片负1会想要覆盖一个没有其他处理器在获取的东西。

sentences.en: So, it would deadlock.
sentences.zh: 所以，它会死锁。

sentences.en: So, it has that twofold.
sentences.zh: 所以，它是双重的。

sentences.en: When you build this processing order, there's a natural pattern to it.
sentences.zh: 当你构建这个处理顺序时，它有一种自然的模式。

sentences.en: So, you don't have to actually build a list, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上不需要构建一个列表，对吧？

sentences.en: You can just encode the pattern?
sentences.zh: 你只需要编码这个模式就行了？

sentences.en: No, I do build a liSt.
sentences.zh: 不，我确实构建了一个列表。

sentences.en: It would be nice.
sentences.zh: 那样就太好了。

sentences.en: This is something that I want to investigate a bit further.
sentences.zh: 这是我想进一步研究的事情。

sentences.en: Whether there's a way of mathematically calculating the processing order without actually calculating it.
sentences.zh: 看看有没有办法在不实际计算的情况下，通过数学方法计算出处理顺序。

sentences.en: I wonder if the processing order, if you can make it like a lazy iterator.
sentences.zh: 我在想处理顺序是不是可以做成一个惰性迭代器。

sentences.en: So, that you generate the list on the fly.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以即时生成这个列表。

sentences.en: Connor maybe can think about the type of lazy iterator that would spawn this sort of sequence.
sentences.zh: 康纳也许可以考虑一下能产生这种序列的惰性迭代器的类型。

sentences.en: He's cranking on it, folks.
sentences.zh: 伙计们，他正在努力呢。

sentences.en: I don't fully...
sentences.zh: 我不是很……

sentences.en: I raised an eyebrow when you asked that initially.
sentences.zh: 你刚开始问那个问题时我挑了挑眉。

sentences.en: And I was thinking in my head, I don't fully understand what you're...
sentences.zh: 我心里在想，我不太明白你……

sentences.en: So, you want this...
sentences.zh: 所以，你想要这个……

sentences.en: So, this sequence...
sentences.zh: 所以，这个序列……

sentences.en: The sequence of the processing order of 0, negative 1, 3, negative 4, 6, 2, negative 3, 5, 1, negative 2, 4.
Like, come up with some lazy iterator invocation that expands to that.
sentences.zh: 比如，想出某种能展开成这样的惰性迭代器调用。

sentences.en: I mean, what's the goal of doing this lazily?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这样懒加载的目的是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the thing is that right now, in the actual implementation, you calculate this processing order on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 嗯，问题在于目前在实际实现中，你是在CPU上计算这个处理顺序的。

sentences.en: And then you allocate an array on the GPU that contains this processing order.
sentences.zh: 然后你在GPU上分配一个包含这个处理顺序的数组。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's what you use so that the thread blocks grab tiles.
sentences.zh: 这就是你用来让线程块获取切片的东西。

sentences.en: They grab tiles according to this processing order.
sentences.zh: 它们根据这个处理顺序来获取切片。

sentences.en: And it would be ideal if you didn't have to do that and a thread of blocks could say, okay, I want to...
sentences.zh: 如果不需要这样做，并且线程块可以说“好吧，我想……”，那就太理想了。

sentences.en: Right now, I want to process the fifth tile along the processing order.
sentences.zh: 现在，我想处理沿处理顺序的第五个切片。

sentences.en: And it would be nice if the thread block had a way of calculating which tile is the fifth one along the processing order without having to go through all of this.
sentences.zh: 如果线程块有一种方法可以计算出沿处理顺序的第五个切片是哪一个，而不必遍历所有这些，那就太好了。

sentences.en: Because then this would be super costly.
sentences.zh: 因为那样的话代价会非常高。

sentences.en: I mean, and it's pretty simple the way that this is generated in that once you have your dependency table of, like, key value pairs, you're just following it starting at zero,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这个生成方式其实很简单，一旦你有了键值对的依赖表，你只需要从0开始跟着它走，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You go from the zero key to the zero value, which is then going to be your next key that you look up.
sentences.zh: 你从0键走到0值，然后这就会成为你要查找的下一个键。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: But it does get a little complicated once you get to the end of this dependency graph, because then you have some entries that have two in the table.
sentences.zh: 但一旦你到了这个依赖图的末尾，事情就变得有点复杂了，因为那时表中有些条目有两个值。

sentences.en: Like, there's negative fours, zero, there's zero.
sentences.zh: 比如有负4，零，还有零。

sentences.en: There's very little that have two.
sentences.zh: 有两个值的非常少。

sentences.en: In real implementations, most tiles would be overriding two tiles.
sentences.zh: 在实际实现中，大多数切片都会覆盖两个切片。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会这样？

sentences.en: Well, okay, maybe not moSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，好吧，也许不是大多数。

sentences.en: I think probably...
sentences.zh: 我想大概……

sentences.en: But wait, why are you ever overriding two tiles?
sentences.zh: 但是等等，你为什么会覆盖两个切片？

sentences.en: Aren't you just ever overriding one tile?
sentences.zh: 难道你不是一直都只覆盖一个切片吗？

sentences.en: No, because here, for example, since our array has a size of three and a half tiles, the last negative tile is going to be partial.
sentences.zh: 不，因为这里，举个例子，由于我们的数组大小是三个半切片，最后一个负切片将是不完整的。

sentences.en: And so whoever overrides it, it's not going to overwrite fully, and so it's going to jump into two tiles.
sentences.zh: 所以不管是谁覆盖它，它都不会完全覆盖，因此它会跳转到两个切片中。

sentences.en: Let's, for right now, I think for...
sentences.zh: 现在，我觉得对于……

sentences.en: If you limit yourself to the case of no partial tiles, then I think it becomes easier to imagine how you could create a lazy iterator for this.
sentences.zh: 如果你把自己限制在没有部分切片的情况，那么我觉得就更容易想象如何为此创建一个惰性迭代器了。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it probably doesn't affect generalizability, I would guess.
sentences.zh: 是的，我猜这可能不影响通用性。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Come on, Connor, crank out some APL or something.
sentences.zh: 来吧，康纳，写点APL或类似的东西出来。

sentences.en: The other problem is also that you don't want to have to generate the dependency table on the GPU either,
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，你也不希望在GPU上生成依赖表，

sentences.en: because right now we only have 10 tiles, but you have to imagine that for an array of a gigabyte,
sentences.zh: 因为现在我们只有10个切片，但你得想象一下，对于一个吉字节的数组，

sentences.en: you have tens of thousands of tiles, and so generating this dependency table would take more time than actually doing the rotate.
sentences.zh: 你有几万个切片，所以生成这个依赖表所花费的时间会比实际旋转还要长。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: So wait, you said you don't want to do that on the GPU?
sentences.zh: 等等，你是说你不想在GPU上做这个？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So this, the processing order generation and the dependency table generation takes part on the CPU.
sentences.zh: 所以这个，处理顺序的生成和依赖表的生成是在CPU上进行的。

sentences.en: And then the array that is the processing order, you copy it to the GPU, and then you do the actual rotation on the GPU.
sentences.zh: 然后作为处理顺序的数组会被复制到GPU上，接着你在GPU上执行实际的旋转。

sentences.en: And you were saying you want to keep the dependency table generation on the CPU, but the...
sentences.zh: 而你刚才说你想把依赖表的生成留在CPU上，但是……

sentences.en: No, I want to find a way of not having to generate the dependency table.
sentences.zh: 不，我想找到一种不用生成依赖表的方法。

sentences.en: Let's say I want to find a way where a thread block says it wants to process the fifth tile along the processing order, which in our case is tile 6.
sentences.zh: 比方说，我想找到一种方法，让一个线程块表示它想要处理沿处理顺序的第五个切片，在我们的例子中就是切片6。

sentences.en: And the question is, would there be a way of calculating that the fifth tile along the processing order,
sentences.zh: 问题是，有没有办法计算出沿处理顺序的第五个切片，

sentences.en: if we start at 0, is tile 6, without generating the full dependency table or the partial dependency table that we would need up until that point, and doing the...
sentences.zh: 如果我们从0开始，就是切片6，而不需要生成到那个点为止所需的完整依赖表或部分依赖表，也不用去……

sentences.en: and like walking along the dependency graph?
sentences.zh: 就像沿着依赖图遍历一样？

sentences.en: That's...
sentences.zh: 那是……

sentences.en: Yeah, I see.
sentences.zh: 对，我明白了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It seems like it could be possible, but it's hard to kind of find the mathematical...
sentences.zh: 这似乎是可能的，但很难找到那种数学上的……

sentences.en: Now, I lack brain cells right now to be able to think through this.
sentences.zh: 现在，我脑子里缺乏足够的脑细胞来仔细思考这个。

sentences.en: However, I think we should both think about this.
sentences.zh: 不过，我觉得我们俩都应该考虑一下这个。

sentences.en: I have another...
sentences.zh: 我还有另一个……

sentences.en: I said earlier, I can't think of an algorithm that's sort of similar to this, but I did just think of an algorithm that...
sentences.zh: 我刚才说过，我想不出一个与此类似的算法，但我刚刚确实想到了一个算法……

sentences.en: I don't think it's similar, but maybe it's in the family.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它不太相似，但也许属于同一类。

sentences.en: And the algorithm is transpose.
sentences.zh: 这个算法就是转置。

sentences.en: And the similarity that transpose has to rotate is that both algorithms are purely data movement, and both algorithms have like some data reuse pattern,
sentences.zh: 转置与旋转的相似之处在于，这两个算法都是纯粹的数据移动，并且两个算法都有某种数据重用模式，

sentences.en: but like at the L2 level, they would have some data reuse pattern.
sentences.zh: 但比如在L2级别，它们会有某种数据重用模式。

sentences.en: However, both algorithms only ever, you know, load each element once and store each element once from like global memory.
sentences.zh: 然而，两个算法都只从全局内存中加载每个元素一次，并存储每个元素一次。

sentences.en: Now, the other thing about transpose that I think is a little bit interesting is...
sentences.zh: 现在，关于转置的另一件事，我觉得有点意思的是……

sentences.en: So, when you transpose, you sort of do like a local transpose, and then you do like a, you know, a global transpose.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你进行转置时，你有点像在做局部转置，然后你再做类似于……全局转置。

sentences.en: Like you load a tile, you transpose within the tile, and then you like write back that tile to some new transpose location.
sentences.zh: 就像你加载一个切片，在切片内部进行转置，然后把那个切片写回到某个新的转置位置。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Something about that pattern sort of reminded me of rotate.
sentences.zh: 这种模式的某些地方让我想起了旋转。

sentences.en: I felt like maybe there was some similarities there.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这之间可能有一些相似之处。

sentences.en: We don't have like a transpose algorithm in CUB, just like a pure transpose, but...
sentences.zh: 我们在CUB中没有像转置这样的算法，没有纯粹的转置，但是……

sentences.en: And can you do the transpose in place?
sentences.zh: 你能就地（in-place）进行转置吗？

sentences.en: I'm not sure about that.
sentences.zh: 这一点我不太确定。

sentences.en: I don't know if the usual implementations do it in place, or if they just allocate a new array.
sentences.zh: 我不知道通常的实现是不是就地进行的，还是说它们只是分配了一个新数组。

sentences.en: Because it's hard to imagine that it could be done for large enough matrices.
sentences.zh: 因为很难想象对于足够大的矩阵这能做到。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, actually, I think if you took a similar approach, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，实际上，我觉得如果你采用类似的方法，对吧？

sentences.en: Like if I know, for any given tile, I know where that tile is going to go.
sentences.zh: 就像如果我知道，对于任何给定的切片，我知道那个切片要去哪里。

sentences.en: And so, I know my...
sentences.zh: 所以，我知道我的……

sentences.en: The same thing, the same dependency thing can be done, I think.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情，同样的依赖关系也可以做到，我想。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the problem is, because I thought about this also for doing a bit plan transpose, which is very similar to a normal one,
sentences.zh: 对，但问题是，因为我也为位平面转置（bit plane transpose）考虑过这一点，这与普通的非常相似，

sentences.en: where you're just basically, if you have an array of characters, you're then transposing them so that you now have the most significant bit of the character,
sentences.zh: 基本上就是，如果你有一个字符数组，你对它们进行转置，这样你现在就有了字符最高有效位，

sentences.en: one after the other, then the second most significant bit, and so on.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个，然后是第二高有效位，以此类推。

sentences.en: And in that case, you basically have an infinite dependency chain, where everything depends on everything.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你基本上有一个无限的依赖链，所有东西都依赖于所有东西。

sentences.en: And so, you always would have a deadlock, because you wouldn't have enough parallelism to cover everything, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以，你总是会遇到死锁，因为你基本上没有足够的并行性来覆盖所有事情。

sentences.en: I don't know if that would be the case with a normal transpose.
